tagline.text: Baroque cathedral of the Diocese of Pasig, founded with the town in 1573

location.label: Location
location.text: Plaza Rizal, Malinao, Pasig City, near Caruncho Avenue

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱0–300 (no admission fee; transport and snacks not included)

children.text: Pasig Cathedral was built in 1573 alongside the founding of the town of Pasig, and it became a cathedral in 2003 when the Diocese of Pasig was created. Walk around the Baroque stone building facing Plaza Rizal, add the city museum next door, and you have a short, rewarding old-town stroll.

Pasig is best known for modern business and shopping districts such as Ortigas Center and Capitol Commons, but head upriver and you will find an old town more than 400 years old. Right at its heart stands
Immaculate Conception Cathedral
, the official name of the church most people simply call Pasig Cathedral. Its address is directly in front of Plaza Rizal in the Malinao district.
The story begins on
January 20, 1572
, when the Augustinian friar Alonso de Alvarado set up a mission parish in Pinagbuhatan. Frequent flooding led the community to move to the higher ground where the church stands today, and on
July 2, 1573
, together with the founding of the town of Pasig, a church dedicated to Our Lady of the Visitation was established. On
April 25, 1587
the patronage changed to the Immaculate Conception, which it keeps to this day.

During the British occupation of Manila in 1762–1764, the church is said to have served as British headquarters, with the bell tower used as a lookout. CICM fathers took charge of the parish in 1910, diocesan priests took over in 1979, and on August 21, 2003, the parish became a cathedral when the Diocese of Pasig was established. On December 7, 2008, the image of Our Lady received a solemn canonical coronation. As the seat of the diocese, the church serves nine barangays, including Malinao, San Jose, Bambang, Bagong Katipunan, Santa Rosa, Sumilang, San Nicolas, Santa Cruz and Kapasigan, and in February 2021 it was named a Jubilee Church for the 500th anniversary of Christianity in the Philippines. With so much local faith and history layered together, this is more than an architecture stop: it helps you understand Pasig's identity.

The church is a Baroque stone building, and its highlights are the front facade, the main altar (retablo mayor), and the restored side altars and baptistery. A seven-year restoration that began in 2015 was completed on March 25, 2022, and the church now shines again with newly added ceiling paintings. It is not a glossy tourist attraction but a living church where locals still attend Mass every day, so please visit with that in mind. Checking the Mass schedule and opening hours before you go will save you a wasted trip.

From Plaza Rizal, the old stone facade fills your view. Built in the 18th century, it is known as one of the oldest buildings in Pasig, and the edge of the plaza is a good spot to capture the whole front. Around noon the sun shines straight onto the facade and photos can look flat, so morning or late afternoon is better.

blocks.title: Main altar and the image of Our Lady

children.text: The central retablo mayor enshrines the church's patroness, the image of Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception of Pasig. Crowned in 2008, it is the center of local devotion, and it is courteous to look at it quietly from a respectful distance.

The restoration that ended in March 2022 tidied up the side retablos and the baptistery and added ceiling paintings. When no Mass is in progress, look up at the ceiling and you can sense the results of the restoration.

The bell tower, said to have served as a lookout during the British occupation, was fitted with electronic carillon bells in 1997 and still marks the hours. An 18th-century bell is reportedly displayed on the church grounds, so take a slow walk around the yard.

blocks.title: Plaza Rizal and the city museum

children.text: Plaza Rizal lies right in front of the cathedral, and next to it is the Pasig City Museum, housed in the converted Concepcion mansion. Combining the church, plaza and museum makes the layout of Pasig's old town easy to grasp. The museum is said to have reopened in March 2025, but check current exhibits and visiting conditions before you go.

The diocesan museum is reported to hold mementos of the coronation. On the first Saturday of every month, the Besomanto (Pahalik) devotion lets worshippers kiss the image of Our Lady, and many faithful gather on the December 8 feast day.

blocks.title: The old acacia at Pasig Catholic Cemetery

children.text: Pasig Catholic Cemetery, close to the church, has an acacia tree thought to have been planted around 1722–1760 and listed as a heritage tree. It stands near the corner of A. Luna Street and Caruncho Avenue in Malinao. As this is a cemetery, please stay quiet and respectful.

items.title: 1–2 hour route
items.subtitle: Focus on the church and plaza

children.text: Arrive at Plaza Rizal and first look over the church facade and the Rizal monument in the plaza. Check the notice board on site to make sure you will not clash with Mass times.
Step inside and quietly take in the central altar, the ceiling paintings and the side altars. If Mass is under way, stay at the back for a moment and then step out.
Explore the grounds and the area around the bell tower, including the 18th-century bell, and take photos. Ask worshippers for permission before photographing people.
Visit the Pasig City Museum across the plaza, or head off for lunch. Check the museum's opening hours before your visit.
Sources differ a little on the church's opening hours. Wikivoyage lists 8:00 AM–11:30 AM and 1:00 PM–5:00 PM, but hours can change around Masses, so check for the latest notice.

items.title: Half-day route
items.subtitle: Combine the old town with modern Pasig

children.text: Observe the atmosphere of a morning Mass at the cathedral, or spend some quiet time in prayer.
Learn about the city's history at the Pasig City Museum beside Plaza Rizal.
Have lunch around the old-town market. Wikivoyage lists a long-running bakery and a pancit restaurant nearby.
Take a taxi or Grab toward Ortigas Center and relax in a mall or cafe.
From Manila (Intramuros, Malate, Ermita), Grab or a taxi is the most convenient. Without traffic it takes about
40 minutes–1 hour
, and in heavy traffic it can take
1 hour 30 minutes
or more.
From Makati and BGC, via C5 and the roads toward Ortigas, it is about
30 minutes–1 hour
away. Avoid rush hours (weekday mornings
and evenings
Exact travel times vary widely with traffic. Check a live route in a navigation app.

According to Wikivoyage, jeepneys leave from the terminal at Pasig's old public market for Quiapo, Mandaluyong, Marikina, Taguig and other destinations. The church is in the old center around this market.
Bus Route 2 (Quiapo–Angono) runs along Ortigas Avenue and stops near LRT Gilmore station. Routes like these can change, so confirm the destination before boarding.
The church, Plaza Rizal and the museum are a few minutes' walk from one another.
For short distances in town, use a tricycle or jeepney. Fares depend on the distance and on negotiation, so confirm before you ride.
Walking along big roads like C5 is uncomfortable and reported to feel unsafe, so take side streets or a taxi when possible.
The cathedral is mostly an indoor visit, but you will walk around the plaza and grounds, so the cooler dry season is more comfortable. Morning is better than the hottest part of the day.
On December 8, the feast of the Immaculate Conception, many worshippers gather and events are held. It is a good time to feel the atmosphere, but it is crowded and a quiet visit is hard.

The old center has few large lodgings, so most visitors stay around Ortigas Center or Capitol Commons and make a day trip. Wikivoyage lists Pasig hotels such as Astoria Plaza, The Malayan Plaza and The Richmonde Hotel; check current prices on a booking app.

Old-town eating options mentioned there include Dimas-Alang Bakery in Kapasigan (said to have opened in 1919), Ado's Panciteria, a pancit restaurant in business for over fifty years, and Charing's Halo-Halo at the market. Businesses change, so check before you go. Around Capitol Commons, Kapitolyo has a cluster of cafes and restaurants.

If the church is your only goal, a realistic plan is to eat lunch around the old-town market and move to Ortigas or Kapitolyo for dinner. Adding local snacks such as halo-halo at the market, freshly baked bread from a bakery and a plate of pancit makes the old-town stroll more satisfying. Hygiene and opening hours differ by shop, so judge with your own eyes.
Worshippers come first during Mass. Stay quiet inside the church and avoid flash photography and loud conversation.
Wear modest clothing that covers the shoulders and knees. Sleeveless tops or very short shorts may not be allowed in.
Mass times are listed as roughly
on weekday mornings, around noon, and
and
in the evening, but sources differ, so they cannot be confirmed. Check the church's official Facebook page (thepasigcathedral) or call the parish office.
According to the parish, the office is open Tuesday to Sunday
and closed on Mondays and holidays. Baptisms, weddings and similar services require an appointment.
The first Saturday of each month, the December 8 feast and Holy Week bring many visitors and schedule changes. If you want a quiet visit, a weekday morning is best.
Combining the church, museum and plaza in one trip shortens travel time. Check whether the museum is open before you go.
Keep an eye on your belongings around the plaza. It is best to keep your phone and wallet in a bag in front of you.
Traffic is heavy in this area, so after you call a Grab, enter the destination precisely as "Plaza Rizal, Pasig Cathedral".
Visitors who are not Catholic are welcome, but it is good manners not to walk in front of people at prayer or make large gestures before the altar. Take off hats and sunglasses inside the church.
Official information on opening hours is inconsistent, so arrive early; if the church is closed, see the plaza and the museum first and come back in the afternoon, leaving some slack in your plan.
During Mass, worshippers' prayer comes first, so refrain from sightseeing and photography and watch your clothing and noise.
Opening and Mass times differ between sources. Check the official Facebook page or the office before your visit.
In the rainy season (June–October), areas near the Pasig River can see flooding and traffic jams.
Walking along C5 and other big roads is uncomfortable and reported to be unsafe, so avoid walking at night.
On feast days and at big events, crowds gather, so watch out for pickpockets and congestion.
Follow the church's instructions on where photography is allowed, and ask permission when photographing people.
An introduction to the whole city that holds the cathedral, Plaza Rizal and the museum. Refer to it if you also want to see modern districts such as Ortigas and Capitol Commons.
A business and shopping district about
20–40 minutes
away by Grab, good for a meal and a rest after the old town.
A neighboring city to the north of Pasig; you can build a day plan around its shoe museum and riverside park.
The cathedral in Intramuros, Manila's old town, worth pairing with this visit if you want to compare Philippine church architecture.
